newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ANGOLA ARRESTS AT LEAST 18 SOUTH AFRICANS--REPORT.
newsitem.headline: ANGOLA ARRESTS AT LEAST 18 SOUTH AFRICANS--REPORT.

text.p: At least 18 South Africans have been detained in Angola in a government operation aimed at ridding the country of immigrants accused of illegal activities, national television reported on Friday night.

The South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) named the men and reported from Luanda that the arrests formed part of a deportation programme called Cancer II, under which the Angolan government has already expelled thousands of African immigrants.
Quoting embassy sources, it reported that the Angolan police were investigating numerous charges against the South Africans, including that they carried out illegal flights from Cape Town to Angola.

They were also accused of failing to obtain work permits before preparing to work Angola's diamond mines and of customs irregularities for allegedly failing to import expensive equipment and machinery through normal channels.
Angolan government sources refused comment on the report.
A sudden clampdown on foreigners began last month. Angola has since thrown out hundreds of West Africans, Lebanese and Indians as part of its campaign against foreign traders.
Senegal's foreign ministry has denounced the expulsions and Guinean authorities has said many of its citizens sent back had valid papers and had been mistreated by Angolan security forces.
The Jornal de Angola newspaper has also reported the deporation of at least 1,050 foreigners from the diamond-rich Lunda Norte area.
